question: Can two mathematically equivalent FP32 reduction orders produce a repeatable training update difference?

case.training_boundary: final RMSNorm output through the actual tied lm_head and causal-language-model loss, followed by the final RMSNorm backward

implementations.candidate: FP32 left-to-right sum of per-token final-RMSNorm weight-gradient contributions
implementations.repair: FP32 deterministic balanced-tree sum of the same contributions
implementations.matched_sham: repeat candidate with the same FP32 left-to-right implementation
implementations.diagnostic_reference: FP64 sum of the same per-token contribution tensor
implementations.later_randomized_configuration: frozen legal permutations followed by the same FP32 sequential reducer; run only if the primary update result is confirmed

invariants: candidate and repair receive identical FP32 operands
candidate and repair have bitwise identical forward outputs
candidate and repair have bitwise identical hidden-state gradients
the only allowed difference is the FP32 addition order used for the RMSNorm weight gradient
FP64 is diagnostic only and is not one of the two primary implementations

optimizer.name: AdamW
optimizer.initial_moments: zero, then evolved only with the balanced-tree repair gradients

tested_effects: remaining direction after same-state scaling removal

confirmation_rule.confidence_interval: 95% interval on the 16 untouched confirmation inputs excludes zero
confirmation_rule.multiplicity: Holm correction across the three AdamW update effects

next_steps_if_confirmed: run frozen randomized-order configuration and matched sham
repeat with natural warm AdamW moments, moments reset, and stateless SGD
run a complete 4096-step paired trajectory without stopping at the first loss difference
stop_if_not_confirmed: Record SOURCE_PREDICTOR_NOT_CONFIRMED for this declared order pair; do not search for a more favorable order using the same confirmation inputs.
